Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The system TDraw is a computer-based tactile drawing tool created to study blind people’s drawing processes and to support access to business graphics, emphasizing utilitarian goals (tactile rendering, access to professional pictorial information) rather than entertainment or co-designed playful experiences. It appears designed by researchers/specialists with a primary functional purpose, with no indication of game-like or fun-first design, fitting mostly utility-first rather than totally clinician-driven utility.

        (5) entirely asynchronous (i.e., chess by postage mail)
reasoning: The study is about a tactile drawing tool (TDraw) where blind participants draw and later explore static tactile images. Interaction is described as exploration of drawings and comments, with no indication of real-time multiuser or time-pressured interaction; hardware even lacks capability for interactive changes to the drawing. This aligns with an entirely asynchronous interaction pattern rather than synchronous or mixed-time gameplay-like interaction.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely symmetrical (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) mostly symmetrical (i.e., undertale's differing NPC behaviors based on previous playthroughs),
        (3) both symmetrical and asymmetrical (i.e., pandemic with its similar turn structure but different character abilities),
        (4) mostly asymmetrical (i.e., tag),
        (5) entirely asymmetrical (i.e., keep talking, nobody explodes)
reasoning: The study is not a game but an experimental drawing task where blind participants use a custom tactile drawing system (TDraw) to explore and depict 3D objects. There are no opposing roles, no turn structure, and no symmetric mechanics between multiple players; instead, the system and the participant have fundamentally different functions (tool vs. user). This maps best to an entirely asymmetrical interaction pattern, akin to a one-sided tool-user setup rather than any symmetric or partially symmetric game structure.
